page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is equipped with 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for vector extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16 instructions.

System memory consists of 64 GB of RAM, establishing a 2:1 ratio of 2 GB per vCPU typical of compute-focused platforms. In memory profiling tests, the instance demonstrated strong bandwidth with cached small-block reads measuring 2,431.45 GB/s and large-block uncached reads reaching 76.99 GB/s. The instance provides 10 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It includes no bundled local storage and features no hardware graphics accelerators, requiring all persistent block storage to be provisioned over external network-attached volumes.

Benchmark results highlight solid computational execution. The instance scored 2,002 on single-core and 16,430 on multi-core Geekbench assessments, placing it in the top 25 percent tier for raw processor throughput. Hardware-assisted cryptographic capabilities are notably strong, registering 38,480.15 in Passmark encryption evaluations driven by AES and VAES instruction sets. General multi-core stress execution achieved 49,187.43 on stress-ng, while web and caching benchmarks delivered 43.52 million Redis SET operations per second and 29.93 GB/s static web serving throughput.

The 2:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-efficient computational footprint for CPU-bound tasks where large memory allocations are unnecessary overhead. However, the absence of onboard NVMe storage means I/O-intensive workloads rely completely on external network storage latency. The ecs.c8a.8xlarge is well tailored for continuous integration pipelines, batch processing, front-end web server fleets, application compilation, and cryptographic microservices.

Configured with 64 GB of RAM (2 GB per vCPU), the instance delivers balanced throughput for compute-heavy applications without excess memory overhead. The system features AVX-512 vector extensions, VAES cryptography hardware instructions, and 10 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It includes no local storage volumes and no discrete graphics accelerators, depending entirely on remote block storage. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-quartile Geekbench single-core (2,002) and multi-core (16,430) performance, accompanied by strong encryption benchmark throughput. The resource distribution suits compute-bound workloads such as continuous integration, web application serving, software builds, and cryptographic processing.
